summary: Proposes regional registrations for Mobile IPv4. Normally a mobile node reports every change of care-of address to its home agent. Here a new entity, the Gateway Foreign Agent, handles registrations locally within the visited domain, which reduces signaling to the distant home network. It is an experimental protocol.

eli5.summary: If you move between rooms in a hotel, you tell the front desk instead of calling home every time. A local helper keeps track, so far-away people are bothered less.

questions: what is mobile ipv4 regional registration
what is a gateway foreign agent
how does regional registration reduce signaling delay

subtitle: Local registration within visited domains reduces signaling delays.

tldr.problem: Mobile IPv4 requires a mobile node to register with its distant home agent every time it moves to a new foreign agent, causing long signaling delays.
tldr.mechanism: A new entity called the Gateway Foreign Agent (GFA) anchors registrations locally within a visited domain, handling handoffs between nearby foreign agents without contacting the home network.
tldr.outcome: Signaling traffic to the home network is reduced, and handoff delays within the domain are minimized, though the protocol is experimental and requires compatible components.

today: RFC 4857 is an Experimental protocol describing an optional extension to Mobile IPv4. It has not been obsoleted, and interested implementers may apply it to optimize handoff behavior within visited domains, provided their deployment supports the required architectural components.

sections.title: Introduction to Regional Registrations
sections.content:
This RFC proposes regional registrations as an optional extension to Mobile IPv4 [RFC 3344]. In standard Mobile IP, a mobile node must register with its home agent each time it changes care-of address, which can cause long delays if the home network is distant. Regional registrations solve this by allowing a mobile node to register locally within a visited domain using a new network entity called the Gateway Foreign Agent (GFA).

When a mobile node first arrives at a visited domain, it performs a home registration with its home agent, registering the GFA address as its care-of address. When moving between different foreign agents (FAs) within the same domain, the mobile node only needs to perform a regional registration with the GFA. This minimizes signaling messages to the home network and reduces the signaling delay for handovers within the visited domain.
sections.eli5: At home, you tell your parents you are at a hotel. Instead of calling them from every room, you tell the front desk where you are. The front desk keeps your parents updated.

sections.title: The Regional Registration Architecture
sections.content:
Regional registrations introduce a hierarchical model within the visited domain. At the top level, a GFA acts as an anchor point with a publicly routable IP address. Beneath the GFA are one or more FAs that serve mobile nodes in the domain. To the home agent, the GFA appears as the mobile node's care-of address, so the home agent does not need to know about movements within the visited domain.

Two types of registration messages are used: regular Mobile IPv4 Registration Requests/Replies (between the mobile node and home agent, forwarded through the GFA) and new Regional Registration Requests/Replies (between mobile nodes and the GFA for local signaling). A mobile node uses regional registrations to communicate its location to the GFA as it moves between foreign agents.
sections.eli5: The GFA is like the hotel front desk: it knows where you are right now, and it tells your home when you first arrive. Your home only cares that you are at this hotel, not which room.

sections.title: Protocol Overview and Message Flow
sections.content:
The protocol operates in two phases. During the home registration phase, a mobile node sends a Registration Request to a foreign agent, with the care-of address set to the GFA address. The foreign agent adds a Hierarchical Foreign Agent (HFA) extension containing its own address and relays the request to the GFA. The GFA forwards the request to the home agent with a GFA IP Address extension. The home agent registers the GFA address as the care-of address of the mobile node.

During regional registration, when the mobile node moves to a different foreign agent within the same domain, it sends a Regional Registration Request to the GFA. The new foreign agent relays this message, and the GFA updates its visitor list with the mobile node's new local care-of address. The home agent is not involved in this exchange, reducing delays and signaling load.
sections.eli5: First visit: you tell the front desk 'send mail to this hotel.' Later: you tell the front desk 'I am in room 207 now.' Your home does not need to hear about the room change.

sections.title: Security and Authentication
sections.content:
Regional registrations require security associations between the mobile node and the GFA, established during home registration. Regular Registration Requests/Replies between the mobile node and home agent are protected using the standard Mobile IPv4 authentication extension. Regional Registration Requests/Replies are protected using a Mobile Node-GFA (MN-GFA) Authentication extension, relying on the security association established with the GFA.

Extensions added by foreign agents, such as the HFA extension, are protected by Foreign-Foreign (FA-FA) Authentication extensions. Security associations between the GFA and foreign agents within the domain must exist prior to supporting regional registrations. Dynamic GFA assignment requires additional security measures to protect the GFA IP Address extension sent between the GFA and home agent.
sections.eli5: Your room key (security) is shared with the front desk when you arrive. Later room changes are authenticated with the same key. The front desk and hotel management also have a secure arrangement.

sections.title: Dynamic GFA Assignment
sections.content:
As an advanced feature, regional registrations support dynamic GFA assignment, where the foreign agent or GFA assigns the GFA address instead of the mobile node choosing it. When a mobile node sends a Registration Request with a care-of address of all-zeros, it signals a request for dynamic GFA assignment. The foreign agent relays this request, and the GFA assigns itself (or another available GFA) and includes its address in the GFA IP Address extension. This mode allows domains to balance load across multiple GFAs.

Dynamic GFA assignment requires support in the mobile node, foreign agent, GFA, and home agent. Unlike transparent regional registrations, the home agent must explicitly support this feature. The GFA must securely communicate the assignment to the home agent, and the home agent acknowledges with the GFA address in the registration reply.
sections.eli5: Instead of choosing a specific front desk, you can say 'assign me to any desk.' The hotel picks which desk should handle you and tells you which one.

sections.title: Backward Compatibility and Deployment
sections.content:
Foreign agents supporting regional registrations must also support standard Mobile IPv4 [RFC 3344] registrations to maintain backward compatibility with mobile nodes and home agents that do not support the new feature. A domain can advertise support for regional registrations by setting the 'I' bit in the Mobile IP Agent Advertisement extension, along with one or more care-of addresses. The first care-of address is the local FA, and if present, the last is the GFA.

If a foreign agent advertises an all-ones GFA care-of address, it indicates support for dynamic GFA assignment. Mobile nodes that support regional registrations but have home agents that do not can still benefit from the local optimization by using the advertised GFA care-of address for home registration, reducing the burden on their home networks.
sections.eli5: Old hotels that do not have a front desk system still work. Hotels advertising the front desk system use a special sign. If you support it, you benefit even if your home office does not.
